# OC Probate Solutions

> Plain-language guides for executors, administrators, and heirs selling a house during probate in Orange County, California. Written by Vennessa Mele, a California-licensed real estate salesperson (DRE #02115354) with Cosine Realty (DRE #01976619) who specializes in probate and inherited-property sales throughout Orange County.

Contact: vennessamele@gmail.com, (951) 313-3816. Free consultations; no obligation.

## Guides
- [How long probate really takes in California](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/how-long-probate-takes-california/): Most Orange County probates run 12 to 18 months. Here is where the time goes, and what you can do with the house before it ends.
- [Full authority vs. limited authority: what it means for the house](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/full-authority-vs-limited-authority/): The single most important line in your Letters. Full authority lets you sell the house without a court hearing. Limited authority does not.
- [Court confirmation sales, explained step by step](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/court-confirmation-sale-explained/): If your Letters grant limited authority, here is exactly how the sale, the hearing, and the overbid work in Orange County.
- [Step-up in basis: why the sale date and appraisal matter](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/step-up-in-basis-inherited-house/): Inherited houses get a new tax basis at the date of death. Handled correctly, that usually means little or no capital gains tax on the sale.
- [Selling an inherited house as-is: what buyers actually expect](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/selling-inherited-house-as-is/): Most probate homes in Orange County sell as-is, and that is fine. What matters is presenting the house honestly and pricing it right.
- [The investor letters have started. Here is what the house is actually worth.](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/investor-offers-what-the-house-is-worth/): Probate filings are public, and cash buyers mail every executor in Orange County. How to read those offers and what a fair number looks like.
- [Multiple heirs, one decision: keeping everyone on the same page](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/multiple-heirs-one-decision/): Siblings disagree about the house more than about anything else in an estate. How executors keep it from turning into a fight.
- [Clearing out the home: a lifetime of belongings, one room at a time](https://ocprobate.solutions/guide/clearing-out-the-home/): The part nobody warns you about. What to keep, what to sell, what to donate, and who in Orange County can help.

## Key facts (California)
- Orange County probate hearings: Costa Mesa Justice Center, 3390 Harbor Blvd, Costa Mesa.
- Full authority under the IAEA allows sale of real property with a 15-day Notice of Proposed Action and no hearing; limited authority requires court confirmation with overbidding (minimum 10% of first $10,000 plus 5% of balance; accepted price at least 90% of probate referee appraisal).
- Creditor claim period: four months from issuance of Letters.
- Inherited real property receives a stepped-up tax basis to fair market value at date of death.
- Change in Ownership Statement (BOE-502-D) due to the county assessor within 150 days of death.
- Statutory attorney and personal representative fees: 4% of first $100,000, 3% of next $100,000, 2% of next $800,000, 1% of next $9,000,000.
- Simplified succession petition available for a primary residence valued at $750,000 or less (deaths on or after April 1, 2025).
